text:
Marisa: Quick question — RFC proposed lease-swap for active/active handoffs, but during our failover sims we've seen lost-in-flight writes when cache owner flips mid-request. Thinking about a "durable delegate proxy" model: instead of swapping lease synchronously, proxy persists an escrowed write and forwards it to the new region (with ack/playback). Any obvious holes?

alex: I like the idea. Main tradeoff is extra tail latency and storage for escrow. How do you see ordering/at-most-once vs at-least-once?

marisa: Good call. Goal is durable-at-least-once with idempotent replay. We'll attach a write-id and attempt dedupe at target. If target doesn't accept due to residency flag, we keep escrow and surface to operator.

devon: What about legal residency? If tenant requires EU-only, forwarding to non-EU would violate rules. Need a strong pre-check or owner metadata.

marisa: Yep — escrow entry includes residency_hint and tenant_consent. Proxy only forwards when target_region is allowed. Otherwise it marks escrow as "quarantine" and emits incident for manual handoff.

sam: Can we avoid a single point of escrow storage? If the proxy holding escrow dies during failover we might lose those writes.

marisa: Plan is to write escrow to a small durable store replicated to local standby (sync write to 2 nodes in-region) and replicate metadata to control plane (async) for visibility. Escrow TTLs are short (minutes) so storage footprint small.

alex: How will clients be impacted? Do they wait for escrow ack? We shouldn't block the API surface for long.

marisa: Client flow: accept write -> proxy writes to escrow (sync local) -> respond with 202 + write-token -> proxy forwards to owner in background when safe. Client can poll or subscribe to completion via webhook/callback. We add optional sync mode for callers that need immediate strong commit.

devon: Sounds okay. We need clear SLAs: default 202 with expected completion < 30s, and operator alert if > 2m. Those numbers drive autoscaling and retention.

nina: For observability please add per-tenant escrow metrics: escrow_count, avg_forward_latency, quarantined_count. Add trace ID for replay attempts.

sam: For ordering across concurrent write streams, we should include per-shard sequence numbers and attach vector-ish hints so target can reconcile without global serial.

marisa: Agreed. We'll piggyback on existing shard_seq for normal ordering; escrow replay will include shard_seq_range so target can detect holes and trigger gap fetch if needed.

alex: What about read-after-write consistency? If we accept 202 and client immediately reads from new region, they might not see the write until forward completes. Any app-level guidance?

marisa: We'll document: eventual commit for default path. If app requires R-A-W, use sync commit or read from origin region until completion. We'll add a header X-Write-Token so clients can route read-through or wait.

devon: Rollout plan? This touches proxy layer and operator runbooks.

marisa: Proposed rollout: 1) implement escrow API and feature-flag in proxy; 2) dark-launch metric-only in staging; 3) small canary in non-EU region for tenants without residency constraints; 4) extend to EU tenants with legal signoff; 5) enable default. Each step gated by stability metrics.

sam: Worth adding an automated evacuate job that scans escrow quarantine and tries manual operator-approved handoff. Could be integrated with support UI.

nina: +1 on UI. Also add audit trail for any cross-region forwards for compliance. 

alex: Edge case — what if escrow forward loops because target thinks it's still not owner? Need idempotent handoff handshake and a max-retries policy.

marisa: We'll include handshake: forwarder POSTs /handoff with write-token, target validates token against current ownership; if mismatch, target replies 409 + owner_hint. Forwarder then either re-route or escalate. Retries cap at N with exponential backoff.

marisa: Example handshake snippet:```http
POST /handoff HTTP/1.1
Host: region-us1.proxy
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "token": "wrt-abc123",
  "shard": "s-42",
  "seq_range": [12345,12347],
  "residency_hint": "eu"
}
```

devon: Nice. Add a short-lived signature on token to avoid spoofing. Tie it to proxy identity so target can trust forward.

marisa: Agreed — tokens signed by proxy key + include timestamp TTL. Target will validate signature.

ops-bot: [automation] runbook-check: escrow_store replication = 2, default_ttl = 180s, forward_retry_limit = 5, quarantine_retention = 7d.

sam: Couple more questions: purge behavior if tenant deletes data during escrow? We should honor deletes.

marisa: If a delete hits while write is escrowed we apply a tombstone during replay; if tombstone arrives first, replay dedupe will skip. We must preserve causal order by using shard_seq.

nina: For audits include replay events: who forwarded, timestamps, final_result (applied/duplicate/quarantined). Export to long-term audit logs for compliance exports.

alex: Implementation tasks: proxy escrow API + storage shim, token signer, forwarder worker, target-side handoff endpoint + dedupe. Estimate? 4 weeks core + 2 weeks integration + runbook/auth.

marisa: Thanks. I'll open a follow-up RFC patch with interface contract and sequence diagrams. For now, we have rough agreement to prototype the durable delegate proxy in staging.

sam: :+1: prototype first with non-residency tenants.

devon: I'll prep operator runbook draft and failure-mode matrix.

nina: I'll sketch telemetry dashboard tiles.

marisa: Great — tagging folks: @alex @devon @sam @nina. Will paste RFC link when ready.
